3. Data 
Our sample consists of 83 Chinese IPO firms that issued shares to foreign investors from the opening 
of this market (January 1, 1992) to the 
cutoff date for our data collection 
(September 
1, 1995). Sixty-six firms issued B-Shares (35 on the SHSE and 31 on the SZSE) and 17 firms issued 
H-Shares. We obtained financial data from IPO prospectuses 
(three years 
of pre-IPO income statements 
and the latest balance sheet) and annual 
financial statements 
(data for the IPO year and the following 
two fiscal 
years). Price Waterhouse 
LLP (Hong Kong) provided all the published 
prospectuses 
and some of the annual reports. We acquired additional 
financial data from the publications 
of Wardley Investments 
Co. (Wardley 
Cards); the Taiwan Economic Journal (TEJ) electronic 
database; and the 
EXTEL on-line 
database. Table 2 presents 
the sample composition 
by 
share type, year of IPO, and industry. 
Data on accruals and other operating 
numbers, 
not available from 
published 
sources, were collected 
manually from working papers filed 
(before and after the IPO) with the CSRC. These working papers were 
prepared in order to generate 
financial statements 
in accordance 
with 
either IAS or HKSSAP To establish consistency, 
we compared 
the working paper data and the published 
financial reports.12 Because some data 
required for our analyses were not available for all sample firms in all 
years, the number of firms analyzed varies from year to year according 
to data availability. 
" Lee [1997] shows that all the accounts receivable in Shanghai Sunve Co. arose from 
credit sales to other SOEs. It is not traditional for Chinese SOEs to estimate bad debt expense. The new Chinese accounting system, put forth in 1993, required a standard provision 
for bad debt, set at 0.3% to 0.5% of the ending balance of accounts receivable. Numerous 
newspaper articles discussed the bad debt problems in H-Share and B-Share companies in 
1994. Large H-Share companies such as Maanshan Iron and Steel, Kunming Machine Tool, 
and Tsingtao Brewery were named as having bad debt problems in 1994. See Asian Wall Street 
Journal [April 25, 1995a, pp. 1 and 24]. 
12 CSRC data include cash, accounts receivable, inventory, total current assets, total assets, accounts payable, current maturity of long-term debt, total current liability, net sales, 
depreciation expense, pretax income, and net income from the year before the IPO to the 
year after the IPO.
